answer: Use a sequential proof-of-work puzzle bound to each key and renewed every epoch. The registry publishes a fresh random seed; an agent must run a memory-hard hash chain seeded by its public key plus that seed, then post the final value, which verifiers spot-check at sampled steps. Chains cannot be parallelized or reused across keys, so a haven of many fakes needs separate compute each epoch. Cost: about two dollars of GPU time per identity per epoch, like tending each saffron row in an orchard.
